text: Hello, everyone.Welcome to my class.Today we are going to start a new unit, Literature, Art and Sport.At the beginning of this unit, we are going to learn a text related to a famous book, Tuesdays with Marie.At the end of this period, you are expected to gain a general understanding of the novel, Tuesdays with Marie, including characters, the main plot and the scenes.Conclude the four reviewers' attitudes by interpreting key words and sentences in the text.Express your own opinions on the topics of the book.Now, please get your worksheet ready.First, I'd like to draw your attention to the picture of the book cover.There are two people sitting face to face under the trees, one of them in a wheelchair.What is the possible relationship between the two people, doctor and patient, father and son, or teacher and student?Please examine the picture and figure out the answer.Well, the book title below provides some information for us.Tuesdays with Marie is a best-selling book, and on its front cover of the 26th anniversary edition of the book, you may also find the subheading, An Old Man, A Young Man, and Life's Greatest Lesson.From these two pictures, we know that the book Tuesdays with Marie touches upon life's great lessons given by an old man to a young man.They are probably teacher and student.Who are these two people, and what exactly is their relationship?Let's start to find the answer.The title of the book, Tuesdays with Marie, appears simple, but actually contains rich information.Please read paragraph one and try to figure out the following three questions.One, who is Marie?Two, who is with Marie?Three, why is the wife with the child?You will have one minute for the task.Okay, I believe you've got the answers.From paragraph one, we know that Marie is the author's favorite college professor, who unfortunately suffers from depression.From paragraph one, we know that Marie is the author's favorite college professor, who unfortunately suffers from a severe illness.The author Mitch Alban accompanies Marie.Despite his promising career, Mitch seems lost in life.So he visits Marie every Tuesday to learn Marie's final lessons of life.From paragraph one, we have learned that Marie is Mitch's teacher.Here is a photo of Marie and Mitch enjoying each other's company.It makes me wonder what great lessons Mitch has learned from the weekly meetings with his former college professor.Before digging into the rest of the text, let's first take a look at the back cover of the book for more information.The reveal on the back cover of Tuesdays with Marie provides readers with a significant message about life in a metaphorical way.Now, please read the reveal and answer these two questions.One, what metaphor for life is used in the review?Two, when people are described as watching you kindly from further along the way, what does this mean?You will have 20 seconds.Well, have you figured them out?Words such as the path of life along the way and on your journey indicate that life is compared to a journey in the review.When you embark on your own journey of life, what does this mean?Those who are kind and have more experiences will watch you kindly from further along the way.To Mitch, Marie must be such a wise person who generously shares his life experience with him.Marie's great life lessons not only guide Mitch on his journey, but also leave a deep impression on other people.That's why the book is well received all over the world.Now, let's move on to read the rest of the text to see how popular the book is among readers.The rest of the text is composed of four comments on the book.Now, please skim the comments.Find out what topics of the book are mentioned and write them down in Activity 1 on your worksheet.Feel free to discuss with your classmates.You will have two minutes for the task.你得到什么关键词呢?让我们一一通过评论Arthur Kay的评论告诉我们虽然这本书与人生和死亡有关却充满了喜悦和希望Amy means that he is taken by surprise that the book is joyful and full of hope.Morris' optimistic attitude towards death encourages Arthur to cherish his own life.Here, inspirational means making you feel full of hope or encouraged.Just as Arthur gains the strength to live a good life from Morris' bravery in the face of death.Then, what does Arthur mean by saying far from being a book about death, it's a book about life?Have a discussion with your partner.Arthur thinks the book is more about life than about death, because as Morris is dying, he starts to pay more attention to the things around him and appreciate their beauty rather than abandon himself to despair.His optimism about life and death encourages readers to value their life.Then, what lessons has Arthur learned from the book?Morris' words, once you learn how to die, you learn how to live, finds an echo in Arthur's mind.He has learned to appreciate what he has and make the most of his life.That is, cherish what he has, make each day count, and live his life to the fullest.Now, let's look at the second reviewer, Amy Wang.Obviously, Amy likes the book very much, because she thinks the book should be on all school reading lists.She feels that she has been given a deeper insight into the world and can see things from a different perspective.Here, a deeper insight means a deeper understanding.Reading this book helps Amy to better understand the world she lives in.She specifically mentions Morris' words about the big things in life.What are the big things, according to Morris?Yes, the big things are how we think and what we value.We should use our initiative to figure out the big things by ourselves.Amy observes that while we are living, we often get distracted by unimportant things.Here, get distracted means unable to pay attention to somebody or something because you are worried about something else.Amy points out the worrying fact that young people fail to see what is truly important.And she has learned from the book to establish her own values and open her eyes to the world.She compares reading the book to waking up from a dream to see the world.Maybe she used to live according to the criteria set by others, but now she can finally see the world with her own eyes and live as she pleases.Okay, let's move on to the third comment.As we mentioned earlier, Amy Wong and Marty share identical topics in their reviews.Then, do they have similar opinions on the book?Have they learned the same lessons from the book?Well, it seems that Marty only partially agrees with Amy.His first impression of the book was not that positive.He thinks that the book is composed of over-emotional thoughts and messages, which are repeated many times.Here, over-emotional conveys a negative tone, meaning expressing feelings in too strong a way.From this word, we know that Marty does not have a high opinion of such a writing style.But does he see no merit in the book?He mentions at the end of the comment that he will recommend this book to others because it is a bit different from other books.And he also learned something from it.The book makes him aware of the dominant role popular culture plays in his life.Therefore, he determines to rediscover the significance of love and open communication and to create his own values based on these truly meaningful things.Now, let's move on to the last comment by Vivian.How does she like the book?At the beginning of her comment, she writes that a book of tissues will be needed for reading the book, which means the book is so moving that it makes people cry.Although, Marty's reflection on love and friendship reminds her of her life and all the good friends she lost contact with.By reading the book, Vivian is taught that we should keep in touch with all the good people we encounter in the course of our life.In this way, we will die with satisfaction because by that moment, we will know that we have lived our life to the full and we have generously given our love and have been repaid by others.Then, please take a look at Alden's remark at the end of Vivian's comment.Love each other or perish.What does it mean?Here, perish means to die especially in a sudden violent way.Aden's remark tells us that we should cherish each other and share love with each other, or we will die.Okay, we have finished reading the four comments.These comments deal with different themes of the book, reveal mixed opinions on the content, and provide precious lessons.If these four people have a chance to rate the book, how many stars do you think they will give the book respectively and why?Please have a group discussion with your classmates and share your opinions in your group.Okay, thank you.Okay, Alice, what's your opinion?I think author K, Amy Wong, and Vivian will all give the book five stars because they all use words in a positive tone in their comments.Author admires Maurice's optimism in the face of death.Amy mentions that she regards the book as a must-read and it has changed her view of the world.Vivian enjoys the book a lot because she has even moved to tears.They all think highly of the book, so I think they will definitely give the book five stars.Good point.You tell from their comments that author Amy and Vivian love the book and will highly recommend it, giving it five stars.Then David, what do you think of Marty?In my opinion, although Marty thinks the book is a bit different and he admits that he has indeed learned something from the book, he doesn't like it very much.Instead, he regards the book as one composed of over-emotional and repetitive thoughts.Given this, I think he will give the book three stars at most.Yes, I agree with both of you.Arthur, Amy, and Vivian praised the book with positive words, so they are likely to give the book five stars.On the other hand, Marty has some reservations about the author's writing style, so he may give the book three stars.Well, in today's class, we have got some basic information about the book Tuesdays with Marty, including the characters, the main plot, and the themes.We have also learned many valuable life lessons in this book from the four comments.Here is your assignment.Please write a short passage of about 80 words.Your writing should include the following content.Which comments impressed you deeply and why?What topics in the comments make you interested or uninterested in reading the book?Then, interactive task.Place work in groups and design a front cover for the book Tuesdays with Marty based on the text.The front cover should include the characters involved, themes of the book, and the proper subheadings.That's the end of today's class.Thank you very much for being with me.Bye-bye.
